issues.body: The assertion `compare_select(&g, &store, multi).is_err()` requires the two engines to return opposite member orders for a raw multi-member GROUP_CONCAT. But the order is unspecified, not guaranteed to differ. Both engines can legitimately choose the same order, and that order may change with dependency versions, hash/iteration behavior, or implementation details. Thus a correct build can fail this test, while the load-bearing property is only that generated queries avoid comparing an order-sensitive raw multi-member concatenation.
issues.fix_hint: Remove the assertion that the excluded query must disagree across engines. Keep the structural generator check that every emitted GROUP_CONCAT is singleton or wrapped in an order-invariant operation, and retain the positive cross-engine tests for those generated shapes. If a mutation guard is desired, test the structural classifier directly with a deliberately unsafe query rather than depending on incidental engine output order.
issues.title: GROUP_CONCAT test requires a nondeterministic cross-engine disagreement

verdict.summary: The new typed-literal and result-form coverage is generally well targeted, and the tests meaningfully exercise ASK booleans, graph results, lexical recanonicalization, and datatype-family reachability. However, the GROUP_CONCAT test encodes an accidental current ordering difference between the two engines as a required failure. SPARQL leaves GROUP_CONCAT member order unspecified, so both engines may legitimately produce the same ordering on this fixture; a dependency update, iteration-order change, or platform difference can therefore fail the test even when both implementations and the generator restriction are correct. This is a major test-validity issue and should be fixed before approval.
